【Do you still remember that winter of 2018? Now ETH’s trend looks exactly like it】

In November 2018, after Bitcoin dropped from the $6,000 “waterfall,” the whole market was filled with despair—every group chat was nothing but “What should I do?” Back then, ETH was dropping so hard it barely resembled itself. It traded sideways all day, up a little and then got dumped. Everyone felt it would keep falling, yet somehow it never broke below a certain level.

Now $ 1884: down 1.7% in the past 24 hours, basically unchanged over 7 days. BTC’s dominance is 56.4%—the market is dead still.

Let me share three signals—see what you make of them:

First, consolidation and range trading. A directional move is getting close, and volume is still active. What does that mean? Both bulls and bears are holding back—no one wants to be the first to run, and no one dares to rush in. 1846 is the lifeline; 1972 is the ceiling. Trapped in between, it’s painfully grinding.

Second, extreme fear. FNG is 25, with the weekly average only 27. This isn’t just “scared”—it’s fear to the bone. But notice: even with fear like this, the coin price hasn’t collapsed. This divergence is interesting. Fear hits the extreme, yet price doesn’t follow—what does that suggest? There are people taking bids near the bottom.

Third, the oversold range. It’s down 62% from the highs—are valuations now truly “everywhere is gold, everywhere is trash”? That depends on whether you believe Ethereum still has a future. The time in 2017 when I got slaughtered—I bottom-picked right in the middle of the slope. Since then, I’ve both loved and hated the words “oversold.”

My own mindset? I really do feel the itch, but this time I didn’t step in. What did the 2021 time when I almost got rich and then gave it all back teach me? Better to miss out than to make the wrong move.

What about you—what are you feeling now? Do you dare to reach in with this move? Or are you just like me—shouting “buy the dip” with your mouth, but your hands are steadier than anyone else’s?

#ETH #加密市场 #MOONDOGECOIN #Market feel

【你还记得2018年那个冬天吗？现在ETH的走势，像极了那时候】

2018年11月，比特币从六千刀瀑布下来，整个市场哀鸿遍野，群里全是"我该怎么办"的绝望。那会儿ETH也是跌得妈都不认识，整天震荡，涨一点就砸下去，所有人都觉得还要继续跌，但就是不跌破某个位置。

现在$ 1884，24小时跌了1.7%，7天基本没动，BTC占比56.4%，市场跟死了一样。

三个信号你们品品：

第一，震荡整理。方向选择临近，成交量还活跃，这说明什么？多空都在憋着，没人愿意先跑，也没人敢先冲。1846是命门，1972是天花板，夹在中间磨人。

第二，情绪极度恐惧。FNG 25，周均才27，这不是一般的怕，是怕到骨子里。但你们发现没，恐惧归恐惧，币价没崩。这种背离很有意思，情绪杀到极致但价格不跟，说明什么？底部附近有人接。

第三，超跌区间。从最高点跌了62%，估值上已经是遍地黄金还是满地垃圾？那得看你信不信以太坊还有未来。我2017年被割那次，就是抄底抄在半山腰，从此对"超跌"两个字又爱又恨。

我自己的心态？手痒是真的，但这次真没上。2021年那次暴富又亏回去教会我什么？宁可错过，不可做错。

你们现在什么心态？这波敢不敢伸手？还是跟我一样，嘴上喊抄底，手比谁都稳？

#baby $BABY  Last night I went to run a TBV test on the Babylon test environment. At first everything was pretty smooth: I staked 0.01 signet BTC, selected Aave v4 as the target, confirmed the signature, and the whole thing took about two minutes. But when I tried to shove the vaultBTC I’d obtained into Uniswap to provide LP, the wallet immediately blocked it and popped up the message “transfer restricted.”
At first I thought it was a network issue.
After digging through the proposal details, I finally realized that this token hasn’t opened transfer permissions at all. The official rules are very strict: vaultBTC is a restricted-transfer ERC-20, purely meant as a dedicated collateral asset reserved for Aave V4. You can’t buy or sell it, can’t transfer it or shift it elsewhere—don’t expect to “wrap it” into other scenarios. This isolation mechanism really makes theft prevention airtight, but it also traps the liquidity entirely within a single application. @babylonlabs_io 

Let’s replay it with real money and analyze it. Suppose you deposit 1 BTC (at roughly $60k by today’s market price) and borrow $40k USDC. If the market suddenly crashes and you want to quickly move your position to other lower-interest platforms to ride out the storm—no chance.
You’re forced to slog through a complicated process: first close the position to repay the loan, then remove the vault lock, and only then redeploy. On a congested mainnet, the Gas costs of going back and forth and the long waiting time are enough for you to miss the best exit timing completely. By contrast, WBTC—despite all the criticism about how weak the centralized endorsement really is—at least you can use it and move it when you need to; while vaultBTC is basically “detained” in the underlying code.

What originally made the DeFi space so fascinating was the modular puzzle-piece style of composability, but TBV as a component ends up as a proprietary accessory for a particular platform. Aave’s big boss Stani hypes it as some kind of “novel Spoke implementation”—but put simply, it’s trading away flexibility to gain tighter safety boundaries.
Babylon’s whole trust-minimized setup is basically tailor-made for traditional giants. Retail users want the ability to flow through different mining pools, but this is more like a locked-term deposit receipt. Once you understand that positioning, you can see why top VCs like a16z are willing to pour in more than $100 million—because they’re serving big capital. They’re aiming to keep assets absolutely compliant and firmly under their control; they don’t really care whether the assets can be repeatedly frictioned across other ecosystems. #eth $ETH

#baby $BABY Last night, since I had nothing to do, I went and ran a test on Babylon’s TBV network. The first half was extremely smooth: deposit 0.01 signet BTC, select Aave v4, confirm the signature—done in two minutes. But then I wanted to take the produced vaultBTC and put it into a Uniswap LP to earn fees, and MetaMask promptly popped up “transfer restricted” with zero courtesy. I was completely stunned.
After digging through the official proposal, I finally gave up—this token is natively born with its circulation permissions cut off. The documentation is very clear: it’s a special restricted ERC-20, and its only purpose is to be used as collateral in Aave. Transfer to a smaller wallet? Go arbitrage to other protocols? No way. Theft prevention is indeed airtight—but that also means your ability to “activate” assets to respond to opportunities is zero. @babylonlabs_io 

Let’s casually do some accounting. Say you put 1 BTC on the mainnet (about $60k at current prices) and borrow $40k USDC as collateral. If you run into a black-swan event and want to switch your position elsewhere to hedge, forget it. 
Your only exit is extremely miserable: first find money to repay the loan, then dissolve the treasury, and finally rebuild the position. With Ethereum mainnet’s high gas fees and painfully slow block confirmations, you’ll absolutely miss the best escape window. People usually complain that WBTC is centralized custody and has poor trust assumptions—but at least when a crisis hits, it can be moved away instantly. Compared to that, this new design is basically putting your funds “under detention” inside a smart contract. $ETH 

In the industry, people used to hype that DeFi is like LEGO—decentralized and modular. Well, it turns out this block is permanently stuck; you can only plug it into Aave’s dedicated slot. Stani wrapped it in a fancy term called “novel Spoke implementation,” but really it’s trading retail users’ freedom for airtight closed-loop safety.
This ultra-defensive mechanism is completely meant as a reassurance for traditional old money. What we retail users want is cashflow that can earn spreads everywhere; at best, this is a non-transferable, locked-in time deposit. Once you see through that, you’ll understand why a16z led the round with over $100 million—institutions are paying big money to buy underlying assets that are absolutely controlled and compliant; they don’t care about our ordinary players’ high-frequency liquidity and rotation experience. #eth

💡 Bearish warning: Geopolitical conflict escalation directly dampens risk appetite. Rising safe-haven sentiment is a short-term negative for the crypto market.

All six of Saudi Arabia’s massive oil tankers turned around and rerouted around Africa via the Cape of Good Hope. They’d rather spend double the time and pay double the freight costs than go through the Red Sea. Plainly put: the Houthis have muddied one of the world’s most critical chokepoints for global shipping, making normal passage impossible. Even Saudi Arabia—an important Middle East player—can only back down and reroute.

One sentence to make it clear
The Houthis blockade the Red Sea; Saudi Arabia’s 6 tankers are forced to detour around Africa—safe-haven sentiment is bearish for crypto.

What’s going on
A report just revealed by Bloomberg: six Saudi oil tankers are avoiding the Strait of Hormuz and switching to the old route around Africa via the Cape of Good Hope. Everyone knows that rerouting around Africa means a sharp cost increase and serious delays in delivery. This isn’t just about one or two countries—it’s the shipping lifeline of the entire world being passively “cut.” The Houthis have been causing trouble in the Red Sea for months now, and now even Saudi home-based tankers can’t hold up, which suggests the situation is worse than we thought. Once international shipping gets thrown into chaos, energy prices will inevitably swing dramatically, dragging on the macro backdrop.

Market impact
- Short term: Geopolitical conflict + expectations of surging oil prices = safe-haven rush intensifies, increasing the pressure for capital to leave BTC. ETH is currently quoted at $1,902.38 and is already relatively weak—when selling hits, it often drops harder.
- Medium term: If the Red Sea crisis isn’t resolved, inflation expectations will rise again, and rate-cut expectations may be pushed back, continuously suppressing crypto valuations.

My take
Honestly, I can’t be bullish on this one. BTC is currently $64,282 moving sideways—looks stable—but once safe-haven sentiment concentrates and spikes after the U.S. stock market opens, it will likely break support and drop. First, watch for a break below the $63,000 level; ETH will likely fall in tandem. If you don’t have any positions, don’t rush to buy the dip—this kind of geopolitical “black swan” hates people catching a falling knife halfway through. Something interesting happened today. A stablecoin called Open USD officially launched on Ethereum today, backed by more than 140 institutions—Visa $V, Mastercard, Stripe, BlackRock, and others are all involved.

In plain terms, it used to be that card networks were just watching from the sidelines, but now they’re directly issuing dollar stablecoins. The most aggressive move is zero-minting, zero-redemption fees: most of the reserve interest is given to partners rather than the issuer keeping it all in its own pocket the way some major stablecoins do today. This effectively flips the entire profit logic of stablecoins.

I think the key isn’t the coin itself, but who controls the payments pipeline. Credit card networks were always the top leaders in global clearing and settlement. What they want is control of the rails, not to make a little spread.

As for $ETH, after the news came out, the market barely moved—around 1900 it continues to grind sideways. Whether a bunch of giants sitting around one table can truly coordinate remains to be seen, but the direction is very clear: stablecoins are shifting from a niche tool in the crypto world to core infrastructure for big institutions. If you get it, you get it.#ETH #复盘

#baby $BABY On a Wednesday night, a former colleague sent me an article analyzing BitVM3. It mentioned a particularly enticing point: “Verifying costs have plummeted from fifteen thousand to just a few dozen bucks—at last the big pie can meet the requirements to do DeFi.” The tech moves the computation process outside the main chain, compressing the per-query overhead to roughly several dozen to about a hundred USD. By bypassing the high-risk asset mappings, native BTC can directly earn yield. Just from that logic alone, Babylon really deserves the praise of a “secure moat.” Its moment of disruption seems to be arriving soon.@babylonlabs_io 

However, when I open the official node setup guide, a bucket of cold water is poured over me. Traditional Proof-of-Stake networks at most require synchronizing a single ledger, but this one has a “dual-load” architecture: it must both keep Cosmos running and mount a lightweight client, continuously processing BTC block header data. The official recommended configuration is extremely hardware-intensive: an 8-core CPU, 32GB of memory, 2TB NVMe SSD storage, plus a 1Gbps bandwidth connection. The minimum baseline is still 4 cores and 16G. The testnet guide even warns in plain terms that using equipment with 4 cores, 32GB RAM, 1TB SSD, and 100M network speed is likely to lead to freezing and disconnections. The terrifying throughput consumption effectively blocks the entry of individual players.

More ruthless than the hardware specs is the face-to-face “funding war” for seating. As far as the mainnet is concerned, only 100 active positions are open at most, and only half of those can receive the project team’s allocated share. Even more striking: the staking amount must place within the top 60 in the entire network to meaningfully participate in network decision-making. Right now, the top ten whales already control about 47.29% of the influence. Even if you throw money at a top-tier server with 32GB RAM and 2TB storage, you’ll still be just cannon fodder against that absolute capital wall. If you don’t have money to compete for rankings within the top sixty, ordinary people don’t even qualify to be runners-up.

This much-anticipated ecological celebration, whose spotlight is on everyone, has an underlying reality: a mad dash for the base-layer bookkeeping power toward the super giants. The front-end experience may be cheap and smooth, but the core network has already turned into a closed-door meeting for large institutions. Is this truly the starting point of application-level transformation, or the beginning of absolute monopoly? Feel free to discuss in the comments.#eth $ETH

content:
#baby $BABY 周三夜里，前同事发来一篇剖析BitVM3的文章。里面提到个极具诱惑力的点：“验算花费从一万五断崖式暴跌到几十块，大饼总算具备了做DeFi的条件。”这技术把计算过程迁至主网之外，单次质询开销直接压缩到几十至一百美元左右。原生BTC绕开了高风险的资产映射就能直接生息，单看这层逻辑，Babylon确实当得起“安全护城河”的赞誉，属于它的颠覆性时刻似乎即将降临。@babylonlabs_io 

然而，当我翻开官方的节点搭建指南，一盆冷水当头浇下。传统的权益证明网络顶多要求同步单一账本，但它却是个“双重负载”的架构：既要维持Cosmos运行，又得挂载轻型客户端，无休止地处理BTC区块头数据。官方建议的配置极其吃硬件：8核处理器、32GB内存、2TB容量的NVMe固态外加1Gbps宽带，最低线也要4核16G。测试网指南里更是白纸黑字地警告：拿四核、32GB、1TB固态及100M网速的设备硬上，极易面临卡死断线。恐怖的吞吐量消耗，直接封死了个人玩家入场的通道。

比设备参数更残酷的，是席位竞争的资金白刃战。主网满打满算只开放100个活跃位置，其中仅有一半能吃到项目方的份额。更绝的是，质押体量必须杀进全网前60位，才能实质性地介入网络决策。目前排头部的十家巨鲸已经包揽了47.29%左右的话语权。你哪怕砸钱配齐了32GB加2T硬盘的顶级服务器，在绝对的资金墙面前也只是个炮灰。没钱去拼这前六十的排名，普通人连当陪跑的资格都没有。

这场万众瞩目的生态狂欢，底色注定是底层记账权向超级巨头们的狂飙突进。前端体验固然廉价顺滑，但核心网络早已演变成大机构的闭门会议。这究竟是应用质变的起点，还是走向绝对垄断的开端？欢迎在评论区探讨。#eth $ETH

#baby $BABY  Today I carefully dissect the @babylonlabs_io  white paper and found that its playbook for handling bad debts is truly unique. In typical on-chain lending, once the collateral drops below the liquidation threshold, arbitrageurs simply rush into the pool to take the money. But that doesn’t work here. When the BTC price can’t withstand a massive drop, the counterparty must first pay out of pocket to settle the account for someone else. As soon as the lending contract receives the funds, it immediately destroys the corresponding collBTC on-chain and issues a settlement receipt. #baby $BABY

Don’t get too excited when you get the receipt—the real ordeal comes next: you can’t use it to withdraw from the original vault. The system is locked down hard. The counterparty has to do everything themselves, and must open an entirely new storage address. After handing in the receipt, you also have to survive a “challenge timeout window” period before the spot assets are actually unfrozen. In plain terms, if you want to take a bite of this tranche, you have to painstakingly repeat—exactly as before—the same cumbersome actions the original borrower used to deposit funds.

Why make it so roundabout? The root is that Bitcoin scripts are extremely rigid. When the position was initially set up with pre-signing, nobody could have predicted that some future “godlike” entity would come to take over the liquidated order—so they couldn’t predefine a withdrawal backdoor. Think of it like a tenant refusing to pay: the landlord can’t just kick the door in and grab the appliances. Instead, they must follow a complete, court-run enforcement process with the contract in hand. By fitting liquidation into this fully symmetrical framework, the goal is to deny anyone a “green light.”

However, there’s one blind spot the white paper doesn’t explain clearly: once this new pool is opened, how long will the funds be locked up for? Money just sits there burning costs. Right now, the TBV testnet is still running simulated assets on the Signet BTC and Sepolia networks, and hasn’t yet been put through the real-world beating of actual funds. But it has to be said: this design forces would-be takers to queue up and follow the rules—it really pushes abuse-prevention to the extreme. #eth $ETH

A few days ago I saw a new chain go live. APR was set straight into triple digits. My first reaction wasn’t excitement—it was a bit of worry on its behalf. The more outrageous the returns are, the more it usually indicates the network lacks stable staked capital, so it can only keep people by continuously minting more tokens. Once the token price drops, the value of the staking shrinks too, and the security budget thins out in parallel. In the end, it turns into a vicious cycle: the more security it lacks, the more it needs to issue coins; the more it issues, the less valuable its assets become.
After researching @babylonlabs_io  again, I think the truly interesting part isn’t simply providing Bitcoin holders with an extra yield channel. It’s an attempt to change how PoS networks buy security. Traditional new chains, if they want to raise the cost of attacks, usually have to rely solely on their own native token. But for a project that has only just started, its market cap, liquidity, and staking size are all unstable—meaning network security is actually most susceptible to fluctuations in the coin price.
The path proposed by Babylon is to make BTC an external economic security guarantor. Through native locking and verifiable constraint conditions, BTC doesn’t need to first become wrapped assets, and it doesn’t need to be transferred into any custody account. It can still provide other networks with a slashing-capable security commitment. TBV further extends this capability into financial scenarios.
BTC remains in Bitcoin’s UTXO and script rules. What external protocols obtain isn’t a piece of BTC that gets moved away; rather, they receive a verifiable collateralized state. For users, they don’t hand over control of their assets so easily. For applications and new chains, it means they can tap into a deeper capital base than their own tokens.
This is also easy to get confused: the output from BTC stakers is external economic security, while the stakers of $BABY  bear verification and governance for Babylon’s own network. The two sets of capital serve different targets. So when I look at Babylon now, I’m no longer only fixated on the yield rate. It feels more like it’s building a layer of a security market—so new networks don’t have to rely entirely on inflation to buy security, and so dormant BTC finally gets a chance to participate in broader on-chain collaboration in the form of native collateral. Whether it can be scaled remains to be seen, but it’s more worth studying than just talking about “BTC earning interest.” #baby  #BTC #ETH

For the first time, asset control and financial applications have a chance to be separated.
So what I want to observe going forward isn’t just the amount staked, but how much borrowing demand TBV is actually carrying, how much of the network is willing to continuously buy BTC security, and whether the liquidation and redemption flows can run properly under extreme market conditions.

$BABY  takes on the roles of Gas, governance, and network security, but whether it can truly capture value ultimately depends on whether TBV brings ongoing collateral demand and on-chain activity.

🔐 Sometimes Ethereum doesn’t need news that boosts liquidity… but a decision that strengthens confidence in the security of its ecosystem.

Security expert Pascal Caversaccio, known as pcaversaccio, joined the board of the Ethereum Foundation for one year on a voluntary basis. He is one of the founders of SEAL 911, which specializes in coordinating rapid responses to hacks and security crises within the crypto sector.

This step does not directly add liquidity to ETH and does not represent an immediate price catalyst, but it places security and privacy at the core of the Foundation’s strategic decisions—especially after its recent restructuring. The board sets the overall vision and monitors alignment between management decisions and Ethereum’s core principles.

📊 The point of contention here: Does Ethereum currently need stronger security leadership to restore user confidence, or will the market not care about administrative changes unless they turn into tangible improvements to the network?

The smart observer will watch to see whether this appointment is followed by real development of protection and incident-response tools, rather than treating the expert’s news alone as a reason for price movement.

Do you see this appointment as a genuine move toward a safer Ethereum, or just a limited-impact administrative change?
#Ethereum  #ETH  #الأمن_الرقمي

content:
🔐 أحياناً لا يحتاج Ethereum إلى خبر يرفع السيولة… بل إلى قرار يعزز الثقة في أمن منظومته.

انضم خبير الأمن باسكال كافيرساتشيو، المعروف باسم pcaversaccio، إلى مجلس إدارة مؤسسة Ethereum لمدة عام واحد وبصفة تطوعية. وهو أحد مؤسسي SEAL 911، المتخصصة في تنسيق الاستجابة السريعة للاختراقات والأزمات الأمنية داخل قطاع الكريبتو.

هذه الخطوة لا تضيف سيولة مباشرة إلى ETH ولا تمثل محفزاً سعرياً فورياً، لكنها تضع الأمن والخصوصية في قلب القرارات الاستراتيجية للمؤسسة، خصوصاً بعد إعادة هيكلتها الأخيرة. فمجلس الإدارة يحدد الرؤية العامة ويراقب توافق قرارات الإدارة مع مبادئ Ethereum الأساسية.

Bitcoin: The Future of Money or the Biggest Financial Gamble?

Bitcoin has transformed from a little-known digital experiment into one of the world’s most talked-about financial assets. Since its launch in 2009, it has created millionaires, sparked global debates, and challenged the traditional banking system.

Unlike traditional currencies, Bitcoin is decentralized and powered by blockchain technology, allowing secure transactions without banks or governments. Its limited supply of only 21 million coins has made it attractive to investors who see it as “digital gold.”

However, Bitcoin’s greatest strength is also its biggest weakness—volatility. Prices can soar to record highs or plunge dramatically within days, making it a high-risk investment. While growing adoption by major companies and financial institutions has strengthened its credibility, regulatory changes and market uncertainty continue to influence its value.

Analysis: Bitcoin is no longer just a speculative asset; it has become an important part of the global financial conversation. Investors who understand its risks and focus on long-term potential may benefit, but those chasing quick profits should be prepared for sharp market swings.

Bottom Line: Bitcoin could shape the future of finance, but success depends on knowledge, patience, and smart risk management—not luck.

Why am I watching fewer candlestick charts, but paying more attention to fund flows?

When I first entered the market, I watched the 1-minute and 5-minute candlestick charts every day.

A single bullish candle made me think the rally had started, while a single bearish candle made me doubt the trend was over.

Later, I realized that what truly influences the market direction is often not short-term fluctuations, but fund flows.

Price can be pushed around by emotions in the short term, but trends are difficult to sustain without capital support.

What I focus on now is:

📌 Is there a steady inflow of incremental capital into the market?

📌 Which sectors are gaining more attention?

📌 Are leading assets staying strong, and can the hotspots rotate sustainably?

Many people always want to catch every move, but they overlook one fact:

Frequent trading doesn’t necessarily mean higher returns. Following the trend is often more important than trying to predict it.

Over the years of trading, the biggest change I didn’t make wasn’t in my analysis—it was in my mindset.

Earlier, I was afraid of missing every up move.

Now I’m more willing to miss opportunities that don’t belong to me.

Because real profits don’t come from every single trade—they come from a long-term, stable trading system.

The market will present new temptations every day, but not every fluctuation is worth participating in.

Learning to wait, controlling position sizing, and respecting risk are often more important than chasing the latest hotspot.

Finally, I want to ask everyone one question:

If you could only follow one indicator to help you judge the market, which would you choose?

A: Trading volume

B: Fund flows

title: 3步算清空投净收益：别让Gas费把你反撸了
subTitle:
你是不是也做过这种空投：任务刷了几周，VPS、Gas 都花了，最后到账的代币还不够覆盖成本？

空投能不能做，别先看项目讲了多大故事，先算一笔“净收益账”。很多人不是没拿到币，而是拿到后才发现，自己早就被时间、手续费和设备成本反撸了。

只用三步筛选

1. 先算确定成本

把链上交互费、提币费、VPS、质押资金占用都列出来。如果任务要求钱包里放0.001枚 $ETH，还要多次交互，就先看当前币价和网络费用。原素材里的实际经历是：买了十几U的ETH提到钱包，途中就损失近一半，最后空投价值还不如Gas费。

2. 再看发放条件

“确认发币”不等于“你能领到”。积分排名、交互次数、NFT持仓、白名单和名额比例，任何一项都可能把你挡在外面。做过轻节点、拿到NFT，也可能最后没有分配；跑了一年设备，最终奖励只有十几U，这类情况并不少见。

3. 最后给时间标价

免费空投并不是真的免费。每天签到、做社交任务、拉人、维护节点，消耗的都是时间。我的判断是，小资金用户更适合关注规则清楚、成本可控、发放确定性相对高的活动；需要质押重金或长期投入的项目，宁可错过，也别把自己变成免费测试员。

至于批量账号和脚本，项目方的反女巫机制在进步，封号、取消资格和长期沉没成本都要算进去。看起来效率更高，不代表最终净收益更高。

下一次准备做空投时，先写下最坏情况下会损失多少钱，再决定要不要点下第一笔交互。

【If ETH drops below 1700, will you sell?】

I’m asking you this question—not because I think it will drop, but because—this assumption itself is part of the answer.

Right now, ETH is at 1877. It isn’t really far from that level. But you know what? I’ve seen too many people set a stop-loss line, and when the moment truly comes, their finger just won’t click.

“Forget it, I’ll wait. Maybe it’ll bounce.”

And then they watch helplessly as it keeps falling.

This isn’t analyzing ETH. This is analyzing human nature.

Three signals—judge them yourselves:

First, valuation. A 62% drop from the highs—down more than a head-on with the market even cutting in half. At a position like this, is it the bubble breaking, or is it reversing to pick someone up? I don’t know. I only know that in the 2017 run, I bought in on a hillside—thinking I was smart. Experience tells me: oversold doesn’t necessarily mean the bottom, but it does mean that people are already losing money enough to start questioning life.

Second, sentiment. The Fear & Greed Index is 25—extreme fear. The weekly average is 27, basically unchanged. This means the whole market is trembling, not just one coin getting beaten. In this kind of situation, ETH follows the broader market—it has no independent trend, and no ability to fall on its own.

Third, structure. 1839 is support, and 1972 is resistance. Right now, it’s wavering between these two price levels. The 24-hour trading volume is still fairly active, which suggests people are still playing—not a dead, stagnant market. High participation of funds— is that a good thing or a bad thing? It depends on how you interpret it: if someone is willing to take the other side, it means the market hasn’t totally given up.

What about me? Honestly, this round made my hands itchy—but I didn’t. I have a position now, but I haven’t moved. With the mindset of watching the show—you know what I mean.

What’s your mindset right now? Are you willing to take this move? Does it make your hands itch?

#baby $BABY It was the middle of the night with zero sleepiness, so I got up and went over again the Babylon project draft that Wang from the afternoon technical department insisted—no matter what—I take a look at. To be fair, this dual-track confirmation concept is indeed clever. As broken down in a Binance Research report: 100 CometBFT validator nodes, paired with 60 finality providers (FPs) that are staked with Bitcoin. For any block to take effect, both camps must stamp it. Just from the model, this mutual-check-and-balance mechanism makes the cost of coordinated malicious actions extremely high. @babylonlabs_io 

But these hard requirements for “joint stamping” turn into the weakest link in the defensive chain. When my eyes caught the line in Zellic’s audit results—“launching continuous DDoS against covenant members”—I immediately broke out in a cold sweat. The battle-tested tactics they exposed are very tricky: all the attacker needs to do is use junk traffic to firmly pin down some nodes, so votes never manage to reach the required quorum in time. Even worse, while network consensus is effectively blocked, the timestamps in the underlying code won’t stop. Once delays trigger BTCDelegationStatus_EXPIRED, the system will directly slash the Satoshi staked by the implicated FPs. It’s as if the attacker crippled the node’s legs, and the system then “charges you for absenteeism,” ignoring the real circumstances and docking your money anyway.

Don’t blindly trust the nodes’ ability to withstand attacks—go read the bloody history of Bitcoin’s defense against malicious traffic. Just in 2025 alone, Bitcoin Core disclosed a string of fatal DoS vulnerabilities: malicious data that can directly cripple 32-bit hosts, delay tactics that can completely knock nodes offline during synchronization, and even “poison blocks” that can incapacitate devices for more than a dozen hours. Even the core development team has to admit that if you want a large number of nodes to disconnect, it’s much easier in practice than people imagine.

Let’s take a closer look at the 100-and-60 combination. The attacker doesn’t even need to break private keys to steal money. They only need to pick an easy target and knock the online rate of either side below the 2/3 warning threshold, and the entire public chain immediately halts. What follows is block stagnation, staked funds locked in place indefinitely, and解除委托 operations basically can’t be recorded on-chain—liquidity across the entire ecosystem instantly turns into stagnant water. These seemingly unbreakable dual security locks—are they really keeping out outsiders, or did they just fashion a noose for themselves that could strangle them at any time? $ETH #eth

content:
#baby $BABY 大半夜毫无睡意，索性起身把下午技术部老王死活让我看两眼的 Babylon 项目底稿又顺了一遍。平心而论，这套双轨确认的构想的确精巧。正如 Binance Research 报告里拆解的那样：100个 CometBFT 验证节点，搭配60个比特币质押的最终性提供者（FP）。任何区块想落地，都得这俩阵营联手盖章。单从模型上看，这种互相牵制的机制把联合作恶的成本拉得极其夸张。@babylonlabs_io 

但这“联手盖章”的硬性条件，成了防御链条上最脆的一环。视线扫到 Zellic 审计结果里那句“针对 covenant 成员发起持续性 DDoS”时，我立马激起一身冷汗。他们曝光的这套实战打法非常刁钻：黑客只需用垃圾流量死死摁住部分节点，让投票迟迟凑不够法定基数。更要命的是，网络共识被堵死了，但底层代码里的时间戳却不会停。一旦拖延到触发 BTCDelegationStatus_EXPIRED，系统会直接划扣受牵连 FP 质押的 Satoshi。这就等于，节点被黑客打断了腿，系统还要治你个旷工的罪，直接无视实际情况连坐扣钱。

别盲目迷信节点的抗打击能力，去翻翻比特币抗击恶意流量的血泪史就明白了。单单在2025年，Bitcoin Core 就披露了一连串 DoS 致命缺陷：有直接干碎32位主机的恶意数据、有让节点同步彻底歇菜的拖延手段，甚至还有让设备瘫痪十几个小时的“毒区块”。就连核心开发组也得承认，想让大批节点断联，操作起来远比想象中容易得多。

再细品这100和60的组合。攻击方根本犯不着去破解私钥偷钱，只需挑个软柿子捏，把任意一端的在线率打落到 2/3 的警戒线之下，整条公链立刻罢工。随之而来的，是区块停滞、质押金被死死锁住、解除委托操作根本无法上链，整个生态的流动性瞬间变成一潭死水。这种看似牢不可破的双重安全锁，到底是防住了外贼，还是亲手给自己套上了一个随时会勒死的绞索？$ETH #eth

#baby $BABY @babylonlabs_io Midnight insomnia—woke up and started researching the Babylon materials that Old Wang had mentioned in the afternoon. When I opened Zellic’s audit report, I saw a warning about the risk of a “long-term DDoS attack targeting covenant members.” I was instantly wide awake.

Objectively, the project’s two-track verification design is a good intention. According to Binance Research, finality is jointly guarded by 100 CometBFT validators and 60 finality providers (FPs) backed by Bitcoin staking. Block production requires both sets of parties to sign off—at least in theory, that does raise the threshold for malicious behavior.

But the problem lies in this “joint signature.” Zellic points out a rather brutal vulnerability: if an attacker uses malicious traffic to block the network—so that one side can’t gather the required quorum—consensus will simply stall. The worst part is that the system countdown keeps running. Once the time is up and BTCDelegationStatus_EXPIRED is triggered, the protocol will ruthlessly deduct the Satoshis staked by the FP even if the delegation never actually ran. It’s like someone else gets hit, but your principal gets forcibly taken.

Don’t think targeted takedowns are some far-fetched scenario. Bitcoin network downtime has happened countless times. In 2025 alone, Bitcoin Core exposed several pitfalls that can crash nodes: abnormal blocks that cause 32-bit systems to crash, delay tactics that bog down synchronization, and toxic blocks that can freeze devices for half a day. Even core developers admitted that taking down large numbers of nodes isn’t that difficult.

So the attacker doesn’t even need to steal coins. Just focus on the weak link—if the online rate of a batch of nodes drops below two-thirds, the main chain immediately halts. All staked assets are locked with no redemption path; liquidity freezes solid in an instant. #baby $BABY Last night I stumbled across a piece of BitVM3 “insider know-how,” and there was a sentence that really caught my eye: “The cost to run once drops from fifteen thousand to mere dozens of dollars. Now the big piece of the puzzle can finally step in and start doing DeFi.” This tech moves heavy computation outside the main network, reducing the fee for initiating a challenge to just a few dozen to a hundred US dollars per run. That means the native BTC we hold no longer needs to go through those nerve-wracking cross-chain bridges—it can directly earn yield. With this momentum, it feels like that chilly “gold mountain” might be right at the point of explosive breakout. @babylonlabs_io 

But after I dug into Babylon’s operating specifications, the enthusiasm immediately sank to freezing point. Normally, when everyone runs a standard PoS node, you just need to watch the data of a single chain. But this project is basically a two-front campaign: it has to keep the Cosmos network running on one side, and on the other side it must act as a Bitcoin light client, continuously processing BTC block headers. This architecture is extremely demanding on hardware. The official recommended setup is: 8-core CPU, 32GB RAM, a 2TB NVMe SSD, plus a 1Gbps network. Even if you try to scale down to the minimum—4 cores, 16GB RAM—the testnet guides already include early disclaimers: running with a quad-core, 32GB, 1TB NVMe, and 100Mbps bandwidth will very likely cause performance collapse or even a crash. The high-frequency read/write overhead from the dual workload far exceeds what individual players can realistically bear.

The number of active slots on the mainnet is tightly capped at 100, and only half of those can receive official delegations. The harshest invisible red line is that your staked funds must be in the top 60 across the entire network in order to truly have a say in the consensus mechanism. Let’s review the current situation: the top 10 whales have already joined forces to hold roughly 47.29% of the voting power. So even if you spend a lot of money to get a high-end machine with 32GB of RAM and a 2TB SSD, here you’re at most a spectator at the hearings. Without substantial capital to compete for those top-60 spots, ordinary people don’t even have the资格 (right) to sit at the table.

If the ecosystem wants to flourish, the cost is clearly that底层记账权 (the right to write the ledger) will rapidly concentrate among a small number of giant players. Retail users enjoy cheap and convenient services at the front end, but the system behind the scenes becomes a private playground for big capital. Is this really Bitcoin’s “iPhone moment,” or is it the prelude to a final march toward oligarchic monopoly? Fellow insiders—feel free to discuss it in the comments. #eth $ETH

Trump fires off tough words, saying he wants to “beat up” Iran! Can BTC hold at $62,870?

💡 Bad news 📉. Geopolitical tensions have surged sharply, and risk-off sentiment has directly drained liquidity from the crypto market.

In the past 24 hours, Bitcoin (the big one) is down 3.1%, and Ethereum is down 3.0%—all the rebound profits from these two days have been wiped out.

One sentence to make it clear
Trump publicly claimed he will take a “very hard” crackdown on Iran. Risk-off funds are likely to panic and flee, and the crypto market is hit first with sell-offs.

What happened
Guys, it’s actually pretty simple. Trump just delivered extremely tough remarks, directly threatening Iran with hardline language. The exact wording is to “very hard” deal with them. In plain terms, it shatters the market’s prior hopes of peaceful negotiations. The probability of a diplomatic resolution is dropping rapidly, and capital markets are now pricing the worst direction—an escalation of military conflict. This isn’t a minor “words-only” spat; money has detected real war risk. BTC has been sold off hard to $62,870.94, and Ethereum has even broken below a key psychological level, now around $1,864.53.

Impact on the market
In the short term, the situation looks very grim. The logic of a geopolitical escalation for crypto is straightforward: mainstream capital’s first reaction is to remove leverage from high-risk assets. The price action of Bitcoin and Ethereum is closely tied to the Nasdaq and gold. Panic spreads—retail traders and some institutions will choose to sell and cash out, chasing U.S. dollar cash and gold. On the flows side, there’s no doubt net outflows will occur, buy-the-dip support on the order book will weaken significantly, and any small disturbance can trigger a chain of liquidations.

In the medium term, if this stays at the level of verbal pressure, BTC might still bounce and sell off repeatedly after the sharp drop. But if there are substantive sanctions or localized friction, crypto’s valuation will keep getting pushed down further, entering a tough period of pain.

My take
Honestly, my view is very clear: I’m decisively bearish in the short term—don’t rush to catch falling knives. BTC is currently around $62,870 with a bit of buy support, but if Trump moves toward more substantive military action or sanctions land, a breakdown lower can happen in minutes. The downside room may be bigger than you think. ETH at $1,864 is only barely holding as support; both the technical setup and the fund flows look bad. My advice: control yourself—buying here to bottom-fish is basically putting your head out to catch the knife. When Haisense’s shares plunged by more than ten points that day, I said that if market sentiment isn’t stabilized in time, once panic spreads into the US stock market, it could very likely turn into an institutional-grade stampede.

Looking at the market today again, the so-called Wall Street AI asset geniuses’ positions are being taken over at lower prices by institutions like Citadel. This also shows that in extreme conditions, the importance of liquidity far outweighs price.

Personally, I’ve always believed that the round of violent volatility in the Korean market isn’t just a problem confined to the Korean domestic market. Korea’s semiconductor industry is tightly connected to the global AI supply chain. If panic continues to spread, it could very well transmit to the Nasdaq-related sectors.

For risk events involving institutions like Leopold: if the losses are only a few hundred billion dollars, they may not, in themselves, be enough to change the direction of the market. What’s truly terrifying is the chain reaction of panic sentiment. Once highly leveraged funds begin deleveraging in succession, passive liquidations, liquidity drying up, and declining risk appetite can combine to form a self-reinforcing downward spiral.

On the surface, US stock indices may still be at historical highs. But if the overall market leverage ratio is high and the bond and financing chains are relatively tight, then what really needs to be guarded against isn’t losses by any single institution—it’s a systemic stampede triggered by a liquidity crisis.

I’m not saying I’m definitely right—only that when markets look complicated many times, at heart it’s still the transmission of liquidity and sentiment. A few hundred billion dollars of “small matter” for Leopold: once the sentiment that a firm blew up is triggered and stampede starts, even Nasdaq can get cut in half.

Don’t think I’m just spouting nonsense all day—everything I say is logical.

So I dare to step in and grab the falling knife multiple times, and every time I succeed—and every time I publicly post about it, showing I’m catching the knife.

Looking at the market today again, the so-called Wall Street AI asset geniuses’ positions are being taken over at lower prices by institutions like Citadel. This also shows that in extreme conditions, the importance of liquidity far outweighs price.

Personally, I’ve always believed that the round of violent volatility in the Korean market isn’t just a problem confined to the Korean domestic market. Korea’s semiconductor industry is tightly connected to the global AI supply chain. If panic continues to spread, it could very well transmit to the Nasdaq-related sectors.

For risk events involving institutions like Leopold: if the losses are only a few hundred billion dollars, they may not, in themselves, be enough to change the direction of the market. What’s truly terrifying is the chain reaction of panic sentiment. Once highly leveraged funds begin deleveraging in succession, passive liquidations, liquidity drying up, and declining risk appetite can combine to form a self-reinforcing downward spiral.

On the surface, US stock indices may still be at historical highs. But if the overall market leverage ratio is high and the bond and financing chains are relatively tight, then what really needs to be guarded against isn’t losses by any single institution—it’s a systemic stampede triggered by a liquidity crisis.

I’m not saying I’m definitely right—only that when markets look complicated many times, at heart it’s still the transmission of liquidity and sentiment. A few hundred billion dollars of “small matter” for Leopold: once the sentiment that a firm blew up is triggered and stampede starts, even Nasdaq can get cut in half.

Don’t think I’m just spouting nonsense all day—everything I say is logical.

Before the Coldcard hardware wallet vulnerability was officially disclosed, 1,196 BTC wallets were drained out, totaling $70 million. The trust crisis in self-custody directly hits the crypto market.

What happened
Put simply, this round isn’t an exchange hack. It’s that the “safest” hardware wallet people rely on just had a major blunder. A report from Galaxy shows that before Coldcard—who actively disclosed a firmware vulnerability—did so, hackers had already moved in advance.

Friends, you need to know this vulnerability requires users to update their firmware in time to plug the hole. But the hackers didn’t wait for anyone to react. They precisely targeted the 1,196 wallets whose users hadn’t updated their systems yet, sweeping all the BTC inside—up to $70 million in total.

The most damaging part is the time gap between the hacker activity and the official disclosure. Big money already got the exploit code and came in to “withdraw,” while retail investors only saw security reminders to update firmware after the funds were already gone. In plain terms: a dimension-breaking attack using the information gap, turning a hardware cold wallet into a cash machine.

Market impact
This hit the market very directly. In the short term, it will undoubtedly trigger a wave of panic. The overall market was already fragile: BTC is down 3.21% over the past 24 hours and is currently quoted at $62,668.96. ETH is also getting hammered, down 2.94% to $1,861.77.

In terms of fund flows, security incidents at this level force whales to re-evaluate the risks of self-custody. In the short run, some risk-avoidance capital may pull out from on-chain, or people may be compelled to transfer their coins back to centralized exchanges to “save their lives.” During this migration period, on-chain transfers and sell pressure will increase, which is unfavorable for the order book.

From a mid-term perspective, this will trigger a trust crisis in the industry regarding hardware wallet supply chains and code audits. People will realize that the so-called “cold wallets are absolutely safe” is also a false proposition. If even a long-standing hardware wallet can suffer a vulnerability that gets precisely exploited, the whole narrative of decentralized self-custody will be dragged down, and market sentiment will need more time to repair.

对市场的影响

From a real-world perspective, once some highly leveraged, large-scale institutions fall into a liquidity crisis, whether they can survive depends not only on whether their judgments are correct—it also depends on whether there is new liquidity willing to step in and take over.

For large institutions or market-making funds, if the consecutive liquidations of a key participant might trigger institution-level domino-style stampedes, then they may indeed be more inclined to stabilize the market and slow down the pace of panic rather than letting risk spread infinitely.

Of course, this doesn’t necessarily mean they’re “saving one person.” It’s more likely about maintaining overall market liquidity and financial stability. In many cases, stabilizing the market is about protecting the entire trading system—not protecting a single investor.

Many pieces of news are essentially data, not spectacle.

So you can see: although the U.S. stock market has extremely high leverage, institutions are still doing their best to maintain order.

When people finish up their dogshit luck, it's best to stop early.

Back then, I held a bit of Ethereum worth a few tens of dollars, and caught one wave of dogshit luck that sent it up to 1000.

My chip cost basis was so low that I really didn’t dare imagine it would rise again. So I started a new round of shorting plans. Later on, it kept climbing—up to 2000, 3000, 4000…

At the time, there was a small group. Several people like me had also ridden dogshit luck on Ethereum. A few of us, based on the value at the time, even had a few small fortunes. But in that round, the worst was someone who was just floating a big empty bet—an A10 nearly A11—who got smashed right into collapse.

That’s also why, in early 2025, people said Ethereum would break the previous high and take a beating.

A bloody lesson…

Remember: when you’re riding dogshit luck, make sure you know when to stop.

是不是感觉 AI 股神的运气不太好？

刚割肉，隔一天市场就出现大幅反弹。

如果从现实角度分析，一些高杠杆、大体量机构一旦陷入流动性危机，是否能够活下来，并不仅仅取决于判断是否正确，更取决于有没有新的流动性愿意接盘。

对大型机构或做市资金而言，如果某个重要参与者的连续爆仓可能引发机构级连锁踩踏，那么他们确实可能更倾向于稳定市场、减缓踩踏节奏，而不是任由风险无限扩散。

当然，这并不意味着一定是在“救某一个人”，更可能是在维护整个市场的流动性和金融稳定。很多时候，稳定市场是在保护整个交易体系，而不是保护某一个投资者。

许多新闻本质上就是数据，而不是热闹。

由此可看出，美股杠杆极高，但机构们还在尽力维持秩序。

而不是当前“卖铲子”修高速公路的叙事，第二、第三阶段的叙事出现时，他们会毫不犹豫结束卖铲子叙事。

从底部做多海力士就讲过，主力不允许超跌情绪蔓延到美股出现机构级踩踏事件，所以后来顺其自然做多美股半导体。

逻辑那时候就讲清，当然也有小伙伴认为不可能出现机构级踩踏。

应该可以明白整套逻辑，市场就这样…

所以今天我久应该收手，最近确实大气运加身…

Today I saw my friend message me at 4:00 a.m.—just three words: “Inserted again.” I opened the K-line chart and took a look: that one fake/clone coin got dumped for half an hour and dropped 6%, then it took another 40 minutes to slowly crawl back up, with the closing price basically unchanged. He stared at the chart and told me, “You got washed out.” And I thought: “If you just go to sleep, nothing would happen.”

After I reviewed it myself, I realized this kind of “4:00 a.m. needle” is actually a well-worn script: U.S. stock end-of-day liquidity is thin, and a few large orders can slam the price down to form a wick. Retail traders see a 5% green/red candle and get swept up, chasing the trade. But after the needle insertion, it V-reverses right away—while the people who chased end up getting stuck at the top.

Last night, I honestly set my stop-loss and went to sleep. When I woke up today, I found out: hey, nothing happened.

So here’s a piece of advice for everyone (including myself): that needle at 4:00 a.m. isn’t an opportunity—it’s a test. Don’t trade sleep for some lonely high point.

【ETH valuation has reached its limit, but the chart won’t give a signal—what’s most frustrating is this】

Last night, before sleep, I glanced at the market. ETH tested the support at around 1814 again.

Honestly, this kind of movement is way too familiar to me. The main force keeps probing the key support repeatedly—doesn’t break it, but also doesn’t push up. It just hangs you there. Once you can’t hold on and end up cutting, it then throws you off the train with a big bullish candle.

Over the past week, three signals have been right in front of us:

1. ETH is down 2.3% in the past 24 hours, but up 0.4% over 7 days. What does this imply? Both bulls and bears are grinding—no one dares to really make a move.

2. The Fear & Greed Index is 25, which is in the extreme fear zone. The weekly average is only 27. I’ve watched this data for three years. Every time it reaches this level, the market either continues to panic-sell for another round, or it turns into a bottoming zone. There’s no middle option.

3. It’s fallen 62% from the peak. Let me tell you: in the 2018 bear market, ETH’s drop from its high was about this magnitude too. In terms of valuation, this is already an oversold area.

But here’s the problem—low valuation doesn’t mean it will jump up immediately. I’ve seen too many people catch the bottom and end up buying halfway up the mountain.

Next week, I’m watching a few things: whether support at 1814 can hold, whether resistance at 1972 can be broken, and whether trading volume can pick up. If it holds plus volume increases, a rebound can come anytime. If it breaks down, then we’ll have to recalculate the position.

I didn’t trade much myself this week—mostly holding, with only a slight top-up. No one fell for a trap, but I also didn’t catch a big move. The key with this kind of market is: doing nothing is better than acting wildly. Waiting itself is a strategy—it's just that it looks like you’re doing nothing.

quoteContent.bodyTextOnly:
🌐 Ethereum Is More Than a Cryptocurrency. It's the Foundation of Web3.
When people first enter the crypto market, Bitcoin is usually the first name they hear.
But behind thousands of blockchain applications, NFTs, decentralized finance (DeFi), gaming platforms, and tokenized assets is another powerful ecosystem: Ethereum.
Ethereum is not just a digital currency. It is a programmable blockchain that allows developers to build decentralized applications (dApps) without relying on a central authority. This innovation has transformed blockchain from a simple payment network into a platform for creating entirely new financial and digital services.
Today, Ethereum powers a large share of the decentralized finance ecosystem. Users can lend, borrow, trade, and earn rewards through smart contracts without traditional intermediaries. These smart contracts automatically execute agreements when predefined conditions are met, reducing the need for manual processing.
Another major trend is the tokenization of real-world assets. Financial institutions are exploring how assets such as real estate, bonds, and investment funds can be represented on blockchain networks. This could improve efficiency, transparency, and settlement speed across global markets.
Developers continue to build new applications on Ethereum because of its strong ecosystem, active community, and continuous technological improvements. As Layer 2 scaling solutions expand, transaction costs and network efficiency are also improving, making blockchain technology more accessible to users worldwide.
However, every investment carries risk. Before investing in Ethereum or any digital asset, it's important to understand the technology, evaluate market conditions, and manage risk responsibly. Successful investors focus on long-term learning rather than short-term excitement.
The future of blockchain isn't only about digital currencies.
It's about creating a more open, transparent, and programmable internet where financial services, digital ownership, and online applications can operate without unnecessary barriers.
The next generation of the internet may not just be connected. It may be decentralized.

这只是我自己的打算。

如果BTC反向拉盘，ETH缩量站不上1890的MA20，那还是诱多，我不会追。

之前我就是手欠，在1910的位置接了一手，结果被第二根阴线闷杀，现在学乖了，凌晨的盘面，等信号再说。

But looking back at history, whenever the market shows such extreme pessimism—voices claiming the entire industry has no future—it is often already close to the cycle’s bottom. Of course, history won’t simply repeat itself, and nothing guarantees that every time will be exactly the same. Still, market sentiment tends to be similar.

Many people think the main players in the crypto market have moved on to the U.S. stock market. But in reality, the U.S. stock market is a mature market with many institutions and strict regulation. To truly make big money steadily over the long term is not as easy as people imagine. Most of the trading fees are still largely captured by infrastructure—such as intermediary brokers and trading platforms.

Crypto is different.

For a lot of capital, what they want is to attract both existing and new liquidity—bring more incremental funds into the crypto ecosystem. When liquidity is abundant, they push high-quality crypto assets upward to achieve higher returns.

Even if the influence of traditional crypto capital declines, it doesn’t mean the market will disappear. As more and more traditional financial institutions get involved, the future participants in the crypto market will only become more diverse.

Crypto hasn’t died.

What really leaves the market is mostly those with high leverage—people who only want overnight riches and have no risk management.

The market will weed out gamblers, but it won’t easily eliminate an industry that is still developing and continuing to grow.

Tether’s Q2 financial report is out: excess reserves dropped sharply from about $8.2 billion at the end of Q1 to $4.1 billion—nearly halving; the first half’s financial results were down by $3.2 billion. In Q1, it still reported net profit of about $1 billion, which implies that the bookkeeping pressure in Q2 must be extremely heavy. A stablecoin giant’s profit decline doesn’t automatically mean USDT is immediately in trouble, but the market loves to use the “thickness of the safety cushion” as an emotional switch. BTC is currently around 62,979, down 2.1% over 24H, and the funding rate is still slightly positive; ETH is around 1,867 as prices pull back in sync. Risk appetite was already weak—add the narrative of shrinking stablecoin reserves on top, and short-term longs shouldn’t pretend they don’t see it.

$ETH 1862, sell once after hitting, and it’s been beaten for several days—still the same script.

In three hours, twelve full sets of liquidity were all negative; not a single one was flipped. Grinding from 1927 down to 1862, grinding for nearly seventy points—money has been bleeding out the whole time, never stopping. In theory, this price should have broken through long ago, but it keeps getting ground right here. Grinding and grinding—when you shoot up, it drops back.

In the last fifteen minutes, though, some people have started taking. A taker buy is twelve times the sell. The buy orders on the order book are 50% thicker than the sell orders, and whale accounts are adding too. Every time it pops, someone rushes in—every time they rush in, they get buried. Previously, when it popped to 1927, a batch got buried; when it popped to 1900, another batch; when it popped to 1880, yet another batch. Now it’s at 1862 again, and someone’s rushing in.

It’s not that it shouldn’t be taken. It’s just that every time it’s taken, it can’t hold. If it can’t hold, it falls back. If it falls back, it gets pumped again. When it pumps up, it gets sold again. It’s the same one script—over and over.

The funding rate is flipping negative; shorts are paying longs. After they pay, the price still doesn’t go up.

I really don’t understand—who exactly is buying, and who exactly is selling. Maybe it’s just that I don’t have the power.

It’s the weekend today, and I have some time to chat with everyone about my recent personal life and trading

About trading:
I didn’t make money on my live account last month—I actually lost money. The community is the same. I already said at the end of 2024 that during a bear market, the most important thing is to survive, and to keep live trading capital at 2–5wu in a bear market, and 10wu in a bull market. As for my trading philosophy: make small profits and small losses—never make big losses, and occasionally, make big gains.

As for my outlook on the upcoming market, the bear market has been going on for almost a year now. This year is already past the halfway point, and these past six months’ market has really been awful. I’m looking forward to the second half of the year. After all, the market can’t keep rising or falling forever—if it rises too much, it will drop; if it drops too much, it will rise. So I just hope the second half has better continuity or volatility.

I miss the old days when it felt like money was blowing in on the wind every day.

Personal daily life:
At the start of the bear market, I often talked about it during live streams. In bear markets, there are windows of opportunity. I come from a humble background. This year I planned to learn English, and today I also went to the school to pay the tuition for formal classes. In the past, when I was in school, I never really studied. Even so, I’ve been gradually getting used to reading whenever I’m free. Even though I read through a book very slowly, I still have to keep making progress step by step. In the past one or two years, when I have nothing to do, I should study more and improve faster. In life, if you don’t progress, your own height will stay the same.
